decision_conditions: Reason : 1 - The proposed hardstanding front garden, by reason of excessive size, design, materials and loss of soft landscaping would fail to achieve a high standard of design, appearing out of keeping, setting a poor precedent and harming the visual amenities and integral part of the Liberty Avenue street scene.  The scheme is contrary Merton Local Plan (2024) policies D12.3 and D12.4.

Reason : 2 - In the absence of a biodiversity net gain metric or other supporting information, the proposal fails to demonstrate that it can demonstrate a 10% biodiversity net gain or that it qualifies for any exemption. The proposal therefore fails to comply with the provisions of the Environment Act 2021.

Reason : 3 - INFORMATIVE
Note to Applicant
In accordance with paragraph 38 of the NPPF, The London Borough of Merton  (LBM) takes a positive and proactive approach to development proposals focused on solutions. LBM works with applicants/agents in a positive and proactive manner by:
"	Offering a pre-application advice and duty desk service. 
"	Where possible, suggesting solutions to secure a successful outcome.
"	As appropriate, updating applicants/agents of any issues that may arise in the processing of their application.
In this instance:
"	The application was not considered to comply with the provisions of the Development Plan and NPPF as submitted, and would have required substantial changes such that a new application would be required. 
"	The applicant is advised to seek pre-application advice on any resubmission.
description: APPLICATION FOR VEHICULAR CROSSOVER WITH ASSOCIATED HARDSTANDING IN FRONT GARDEN. REPLACEMENT OF FRONT AND REAR WINDOWS WITH LIKE-FOR-LIKE DOUBLE GLAZED WINDOWS AND ERECTION OF BOUNDARY FENCE WITH GATE IN FRONT GARDEN.
